[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Merrill Lynch was a major independent investment bank and wealth management firm before Bank of America acquired it in a deal announced in September 2008 amid the global financial crisis, with the transaction closing January 1, 2009. Rather than disappearing, the Merrill Lynch name and the shorter Merrill brand have continued to operate within Bank of Americas wealth management division in the years since, similar in pattern to how AT&T Corp and CenturyLink continued operating as legacy names within larger corporate structures elsewhere in this registry, though this registry has not established that Merrill Lynchs New York data center facility is the same underlying legal entity relationship as those cross-linked duplicate cases, so no duplicate_of link has been applied here. This registrys search for facility-level detail on Merrill Lynchs New York data center returned primarily Bank of America retail banking branch locations rather than data center infrastructure information, so the facilitys specific address, capacity, and technical specifications remain not published as of the research date. Consistent with other financial institutions in this registry, this facility is presumed to support internal banking and wealth management technology operations rather than functioning as commercial colocation space. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.
